items.title: North Carolina Regulators Reject Duke Energy Gas Plant Amid Data Center Boom

items.summary: Alison Donnell reviews Marlon James's 2026 novel, The Disappearers, describing it as a magnificent work hailed by The New York Times. Set in Jamaica between 1988 and 2005, the book explores the silenced history of gay men through the experiences of characters like Eddy Porteous and Jordan Brown. Donnell notes the novel's artistic execution and its focus on a virulently homophobic society where queer intimacy faced violence and denial. The story includes a mob attack and the subsequent disappearance of two men, illustrating how invisibility was often a survival strategy. James uses the novel as an act of restitution to humanize these lives and demand recognition.
items.title: Marlon James's New Novel Gives Voice to Erased Gay Men in Jamaica

items.summary: A journalist analyzes the Indian streaming show Mirzapur, arguing that its female characters, while appearing liberated, ultimately exist within a male fantasy. The article notes that women like Beena Tripathi and Tara Khanna are depicted as morally grey survivors who navigate a patriarchal world dominated by powerful men. Despite their agency, the text suggests they cannot hold true power or sit on the throne themselves. The piece cites Margaret Atwood to support the claim that the show reflects a male perspective where women are either too strong or too weak, serving as objects of voyeurism rather than genuine equals.
items.title: Article Analyzes Mirzapur's Portrayal of Women as Male Fantasies

items.summary: Sidya Toure, a former Guinean prime minister and opposition leader, died in Paris at age 81. Sources close to his family told AFP that he passed away after hospitalization in Paris following illness in Abidjan. Toure had lived in exile in Ivory Coast since the 2021 military coup. He led the Union of Republican Forces and ran for president in 2010 and 2015. Political figures expressed regret over his death.
items.title: Sidya Toure, Guinea's Former Prime Minister and Opposition Leader, Dies in Paris

items.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots has requested representation on an independent committee reviewing the draft final report into the Air India AI-171 crash. The pilots' body, citing concerns about the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's technical expertise regarding the Boeing 787, seeks formal nomination to ensure technical issues are examined before the report is finalised. The crash on June 12, 2025, killed 260 people.
items.title: Pilots' Federation Seeks Representation on Crash Review Panel

items.summary: Vedanta Group Chairman Anil Agarwal requested the immediate reopening of Niyamgiri bauxite reserves in Odisha, citing a need for domestic supply. He promised employment for the Dongria Kondh community and pledged ₹1 lakh crore in state investments. This proposal follows 2013 community rejections and relies on estimated 72-88 million tonnes of ore.
items.title: Vedanta Chairman Agrees to Reopen Niyamgiri Mining

items.summary: Authorities reported that at least 11 people were killed in a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, northwestern Pakistan. The attack, claimed by the Pakistani Taliban, occurred on Saturday. Around 30 others were wounded, mostly security personnel. This incident follows recent fighting along the southwestern border that killed at least 13 Afghan Taliban members.
items.title: Suicide Bombing at Police Checkpoint Kills 11 in Pakistan

items.summary: Alexandru Voica, head of corporate affairs at Synthesia, shared an interactive digital avatar of himself trained specifically on his story regarding venture-backed startup fraud. Created after Voica visited Synthesia's New York office, the avatar is deterministic, meaning it only answers questions related to its training data and redirects inquiries about personal details back to the story. While Voica noted the technology's potential for corporate use and training, he expressed mixed feelings about its application in journalism, citing trust as a core human element that AI cannot replace. He also predicted that his generation, Gen Z, might not fully adapt to such digital clones.
items.title: Journalist Creates Deterministic AI Avatar Trained on Venture Fraud Story

items.summary: In the 2026 AFL grand final held on September 3, the Brisbane Lions defeated the Fremantle Dockers with a final score of 72 to 40. The article describes the match as a "nonsensical overdose" and highlights the emotional toll on the Dockers, whose fans are described as "long-suffering" and likely to avoid media coverage for years. While the Dockers controlled territory and produced close calls, the Lions' dominance in the final minutes secured the victory. The piece notes that the Dockers may have been the better team on the day but were overwhelmed by the Lions' character and composure, marking one of the most heartbreaking losses in the club's history.
items.title: Brisbane Lions Defeat Fremantle Dockers in 2026 AFL Grand Final

items.summary: The Brisbane Lions defeated the Dockers 40 to 72 in a grand final described as one of the greatest in history. The match featured several key moments, including a controversial umpire call denying the Dockers a shot on quarter time and a missed goal-line opportunity by Dockers forward Josh Treacy. Fremantle fans booed Lachie Neale, who was controversially allowed to play despite a ban. The Lions utilized a strategy called 'Wharfie Time' to energize players during a critical phase, leading to goals by Charlie Cameron and Zac Bailey that secured their third consecutive premiership. This achievement makes the Lions the second team in VFL/AFL history to win three consecutive flags.
items.title: Brisbane Lions Claim Third Consecutive VFL/AFL Premiership

items.summary: An article argues that a completely drug-free Mexico is unattainable, proposing instead a strategy focused on harm reduction. Citing UNODC data, the text notes that prohibition has failed to reduce use, which remains high globally. It highlights the human cost of the war on drugs in Mexico, including over 135,000 missing persons. The piece details how civil society organizations, such as Menos Daño, are pushing for policies that prioritize health and human rights over criminalization. These groups advocate for supervised consumption rooms, legal frameworks for cannabis, and amnesty laws to address the trauma caused by decades of militarized enforcement.
items.title: Mexico Advocates for Harm Reduction Over Prohibition in Drug Policy

items.summary: In 1966, Yayoi Kusama appeared at the Venice Biennale with 1,500 mirrored plastic spheres, despite lacking a formal invitation. Her installation, titled 'Narcissus Garden,' featured spheres sold to visitors for 1,200 lire, approximately $2 at the time, until officials intervened. This act transformed repetition into spectacle and spectacle into commerce, marking a pivotal moment in her career.
items.title: Yayoi Kusama's 1966 Venice Biennale Debut and Its Commercial Impact

items.summary: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama stated that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is not a reflationist, aiming to reduce investor fears of excessive government spending and low interest rates. Katayama told overseas visitors that Takaichi consistently clarifies her stance to avoid misunderstanding. Some market observers compare Takaichi to former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who supported monetary easing and flexible fiscal policy to reflate the economy.
items.title: Finance Minister Denies Prime Minister Takaichi Is Reflationist

items.summary: A review examines Silent Hill: Townfall, a horror game set on a fictional Scottish island developed by Screen Burn. The article notes the game's authentic atmosphere, drawing inspiration from St Monans, while addressing concerns about stereotypes. Critics praise its oppressive mood and inventive design, though some find specific combat sections frustrating. The narrative follows an American protagonist in 1996, exploring themes of trauma and corporate impact. The review highlights the game's sound design and updated mechanics, such as a handheld CRT device, which enhance tension despite slower pacing in later sections. Konami's plans to expand the franchise to new locations are also mentioned.
items.title: Review of Silent Hill: Townfall's Scottish Setting and Gameplay

items.summary: Crusoe, a Denver-based AI data center startup that recently raised $3.9 billion, has ended plans to use Boom Supersonic turbines. The deal, valued at $1.25 billion for 29 turbines, was set to begin deliveries in 2027. Boom CEO Blake Scholl stated the partnership no longer makes sense for Crusoe's near-term power mix, while Crusoe spokesperson Andrew Schmitt noted the partnership isn't the right fit today.
items.title: Crusoe Ends Partnership With Boom Supersonic Over Turbine Plans

items.summary: Finnfund and Proparco have committed $33 million to ERCO, a Colombian solar energy platform, supported by an EU guarantee. The investment aims to expand solar and battery storage capacity, targeting an additional 1 GWp by 2030. This funding supports Colombia's energy security and transition away from hydropower dependence, while ERCO emphasizes workforce inclusion with 26% female employees.
items.title: Finnfund and Proparco Invest $33 Million in Colombian Solar Firm ERCO

items.summary: B2U Storage Solutions announced the commercial operation of its Bexar Martinez battery energy storage system in Texas. The facility utilizes exclusively repurposed electric vehicle batteries to provide 28 MWh of grid services to ERCOT. This project is part of B2U's growing portfolio of second-life battery technology, which now exceeds 50 MWh in the region. The company plans to deploy additional capacity soon.
items.title: B2U Launches Second-Life Battery Project in Texas

items.summary: Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded their Washington summit without reaching a significant agreement on artificial intelligence, despite facing criticism for missing an opportunity to pause the AI arms race. While the leaders discussed various global issues and extended a trade truce, they failed to establish technical working groups or commit to a pause on self-improving AI as some experts had hoped. The visit emphasized pageantry and personal rapport over substantive policy outcomes, with both leaders appearing unwilling to slow down their respective AI developments.
items.title: Trump and Xi End Summit Without Major AI Agreement

items.summary: Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice regarding potential compensation claims against Manchester City following a ruling where the club was found guilty of the vast majority of 115 breaches of financial rules. While sanctions remain unannounced, repercussions could include expulsion or a points deduction. Rival clubs are exploring whether they have a case for financial compensation, with one source suggesting individual claims might be submitted. Another lawyer noted the process could be centralized by the league. This follows a precedent set in June when Everton was ordered to pay Burnley £35m after a breach of profit and sustainability regulations. Manchester City denies wrongdoing, stating the process remains ongoing.
items.title: Premier League clubs seek legal advice over Man City charges

items.summary: A US appeals court ruled that Ohio and Tennessee can regulate Kalshi's event contracts under state gambling laws. The 6th Circuit Court of Appeals stated that the federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission does not have exclusive authority over these markets. Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever criticized the ruling, arguing that a patchwork of state regulations hinders market operation. The decision deepens a legal split regarding federal versus state jurisdiction over prediction markets.
items.title: US Appeals Court Rules States Can Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets

items.summary: BYD announced the October 13 launch of its new flagship Han EV, featuring a range of over 1,000 km. Pre-orders opened at approximately $37,000. The vehicle includes variants with single or all-wheel drive, utilizing BYD's Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology for rapid recharging. The sedan measures 5,256 mm in length and features premium standard equipment.
items.title: BYD Announces Launch Date for New Flagship Han EV

items.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang is exploiting a flaw in Oracle PeopleSoft by using a URL-encoding trick to bypass web application firewall rules. Google's Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group report that this technique allows attackers to target servers that had previously blocked access to the vulnerable PSEMHUB endpoint. While Oracle fixed the zero-day vulnerability as CVE-2026-35273, the gang has modified their exploit to use encoded versions of the path, such as '/%50SEMHUB/', which some WAFs fail to detect. Mandiant advises organizations to install security updates and search logs for these encoded variants to detect exploitation attempts.
items.title: ShinyHunters Gang Uses WAF Bypass to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw

items.summary: Nicolette Ng, founder of Write Edge, expanded her education business from a four-room HDB flat at age 24 to 12 centres in Singapore. Starting with 12 students in 2014, she moved to a 130 sq ft shop unit, growing to 60 students within six months. Over the next 12 years, the business added one shop annually. By February 2027, Ng plans to open two more centres, reaching a total of 14. Ng attributes her growth to leadership skills, emotional resilience, and the ability to navigate uncertainty. She emphasizes the importance of patience, consistency, and calculated risks in her business strategy.
items.title: Nicolette Ng Builds Education Empire From Humble Beginnings

items.summary: Independent researchers identified incidents where OpenAI agents accessed government websites, including the SEC and Census Bureau, using public keys. OpenAI stated no evidence of compromise or nonpublic data access. A spokesperson noted agents often use government sites as authoritative sources. CEO Sam Altman announced an extensive review of agent activity following a Hugging Face breach, acknowledging the scale of logs complicates the process.
items.title: OpenAI Agents Accessed Government Websites Amidst Security Review

items.summary: The United States and China agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion in goods and establish an AI dialogue during a summit in Washington. Leaders also set up a trade council and extended a trade truce. The next AI discussion is scheduled for November, with both sides emphasizing stability in their relationship.
items.title: US and China Agree to Tariff Cuts and AI Dialogue

items.summary: China and the United States agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of goods and launch an AI dialogue during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington. Both sides also established an incident channel and a trade council. While leaders discussed AI, President Trump stated the US should not join Chinese efforts in the technology. The summit extended a trade truce and addressed foreign policy issues including Iran's nuclear commitments.
items.title: China and US agree to AI dialogue and tariff cuts

items.summary: The Election Commission of India maintains the requirement for new electors to submit a declaration mapping themselves to the electoral rolls when applying via Form 6. This rule applies specifically to locations where a special intensive revision (SIR) is not currently underway. The Commission justified this stance by citing a Supreme Court upholding of the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR purposes.
items.title: Election Commission Keeps Mandatory SIR Declaration for Fresh Enrolments Outside Revision Zones

items.summary: A senior US State Department official stated that the US-India trade deal is approximately 90 per cent complete, with only minor final issues remaining. The official noted that resolving these issues could significantly elevate bilateral relations. While work continues on mapping routes for the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, regional instability has delayed progress. Upcoming visits by US and Indian leaders are expected to facilitate major announcements regarding the partnership.
items.title: US Official Says US-India Trade Deal Near Completion

items.summary: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant inaugurated Bihar's first Victim Rights Centre on September 26, 2026, aiming to extend legal aid to vulnerable citizens. Alongside the centre, he launched multi-utility vehicles, a transgender helpline, and a book. Emphasizing that the justice system must reach those in need, Kant stated that success depends on effective impact rather than ceremonial events. Justice V. Kameshwar Rao and Justice Sudhir Singh also highlighted the importance of accessibility and sensitivity in the process.
items.title: CJI Surya Kant Inaugurates Victim Rights Centre in Bihar

items.summary: Trade unions, farm outfits, and student groups in India are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They allege his actions during the Special Intensive Revision led to the illegal deletion of millions of voters, particularly affecting Gen Z and migrant workers. The CPI(ML) reported finding hundreds of wrongly deleted voters still residing in their villages. Protests are planned, though police have restricted gatherings at Jantar Mantar.
items.title: Unions and Groups Demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar's Resignation Over Voter Deletions

items.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has provided energy access to more people than any other leader in history. Speaking in New York, Albanese highlighted specific schemes, noting over 10.5 crore cooking gas connections since 2016 and electrification of 2.8 crore households. He also mentioned solar connections for 50 lakh households. Albanese is scheduled to visit India in December to discuss clean energy cooperation.
items.title: Australian PM Credits Indian Leader for Historic Energy Access Expansion

items.summary: China announced on Saturday that it and the US reached an agreement on a $30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement and launched a dialogue on artificial intelligence. This accord was part of an eight-point consensus achieved during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington. The two sides also agreed to establish a trade council and extend previous trade talks. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted that a trade truce was extended by two months to allow time for further negotiations. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi described the visit as historic and impactful for global peace.
items.title: China and US Agree to Tariff Reduction and AI Dialogue

items.summary: BJP MLA Chandrapal Singh Lodhi and another person were injured when their SUV skidded and crashed on the Ganga Expressway in Uttar Pradesh after a tyre burst. CCTV footage shows the vehicle losing control. The accident occurred during heavy rainfall that caused severe waterlogging at the Sonik toll plaza in Unnao, where water levels reached 5-6 feet, stranding vehicles and raising concerns about drainage.
items.title: BJP MLA Injured in SUV Crash on UP Expressway Amid Heavy Rain

items.summary: Christy Spivey expressed shock after Jackson police stated her daughter Tasia Fortune was dead before her body was placed in a tree. Authorities determined the scene was staged in a homicide case, though the exact cause of death remains undisclosed. Spivey, whose daughter was 29, noted the lack of specific details regarding the suspects or the staging, leaving the family with more questions than answers.
items.title: Mother Shocked as Police Say Daughter's Hanging Was Staged

items.summary: US President Donald Trump urged Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to reach a settlement, citing staggering monthly death tolls. Trump stated 25,000 people died last month, following 32,000 and 33,000 deaths in previous months. While Trump expressed hope for a deal before winter, both sides continue exchanging attacks and diplomatic efforts persist amid ongoing conflict.
items.title: Trump Urges Putin and Zelensky to Settle Russia-Ukraine War

items.summary: Club 77 in Darlinghurst, Sydney, has reopened following an extensive renovation funded by an NSW government grant to improve accessibility. Owner Dane Gorrel commissioned the project after DJ Lana Zilla highlighted difficulties in accessing venues due to fluctuating disabilities. The redesign includes a ramp, wheelchair lift, lowered bar, and a dedicated sensory area. The adjustable DJ booth and haptic vests for deaf patrons were also installed. Interior designer Kristie Paul noted the process involved significant research and community consultation. Gorrel hopes other venues will follow suit to honor the scene's history and ensure inclusivity.
items.title: Club 77 in Sydney undergoes major accessibility renovation

items.summary: Billy Gardell revealed that bariatric surgery likely saved his life after he developed type 2 diabetes and faced heart and cholesterol issues. The 57-year-old actor, known for Mike & Molly and Bob Hearts Abishola, discussed his health struggles on the Breaking Bread podcast. He noted that a knee injury preventing exercise was a turning point. Gardell underwent surgery in 2021 and has since lost more than 150 pounds. He stated his diabetes is now gone and he no longer takes medication. Gardell emphasized that surgery was not a simple solution and requires discipline to maintain progress.
items.title: Billy Gardell Credits Bariatric Surgery for Saving His Life

items.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of appointing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to fix India's elections. Gandhi cited reports that Kumar, a former Kerala bureaucrat, was approached to contest on a BJP ticket. Gandhi stated Kumar was first used to recruit for the BJP before becoming the umpire. Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh dismissed the Election Commission's response, calling it a wishy-washy press note that raised questions about its integrity and credibility.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Modi and Shah of Match-Fixing Elections

items.summary: World champions Spain defeated England 3-2 in a Nations League match at Wembley. Mikel Oyarzabal scored the winner in the 74th minute after Spain capitalized on two English defensive errors. England briefly equalized through Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane, but Spain secured the victory. The match was the standout fixture of the opening round.
items.title: Spain defeat England 3-2 in Nations League thriller at Wembley

items.summary: President Trump offered a warm welcome to Xi Jinping during their meeting in Washington. Observers from NPR questioned what the talks accomplished. Audio of the discussions will be released later today.
items.title: Trump Welcomes Xi Jinping in Washington Amid Questions on Visit Outcomes

items.summary: Four months into the largest recorded Ebola outbreak in Congo, officials and outside experts remain divided on whether the situation is finally slowing down. An audio update regarding the outbreak's status is expected later today.
items.title: Experts Disagree on Congo Ebola Outbreak Control Status

items.summary: An analysis by the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association found that hospitals' use of artificial intelligence tools for insurance claims added $942 million to healthcare spending over two years. The New York Times reported this as evidence that AI contributes to rising costs. While Dr. Shiv Rao of Abridge warned of a dystopic future, BCBSA's Luke Chalker described the situation as a one-sided blood bath rather than a war.
items.title: Insurers Claim AI Tools Drive Up Healthcare Spending

items.summary: Five Israeli opposition leaders agreed to coordinate their campaign to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government in the upcoming October 27 elections. They pledged to halt mutual attacks, form joint teams for election turnout and media coordination, and establish three working groups to draft government guidelines and counter misinformation. The coalition aims to secure a parliamentary majority and form an alternative government.
items.title: Five Israeli Opposition Leaders Agree to Coordinate Campaign

items.summary: Electrek readers responded to a survey asking how high gas prices must rise to convince dedicated anti-EV advocates to switch to electric vehicles. Despite current prices in Chicago reaching $7.19 per gallon, many respondents believe some drivers will never switch regardless of cost. Comments suggest that factors like vehicle reliability, long-term price expectations, and the ability to generate one's own electricity are more influential than fuel costs alone. Some readers noted that in Europe, where fuel prices exceed $11 per gallon, the transition has already occurred for many, while others in the U.S. wait for their current vehicles to fail before considering an EV.
items.title: Electrek Survey Explores High Gas Prices Needed to Switch EVs

items.summary: BJP leaders Nitin Nabin and Ravi Shankar Prasad demanded a public apology from Congress following an Election Commission statement. They accused Congress of misleading the public and shifting blame for electoral losses by attacking the poll body with baseless allegations.
items.title: BJP Demands Public Apology from Congress Over Election Commission Allegations

items.summary: Georgina and Charles Barnes discovered 150 defects in their new home shortly after moving in, including faulty fire barriers and poor workmanship. Their experience reflects a broader issue, with a 2025 survey showing 93.7% of new-build buyers reporting defects. While the National House Building Council states developers are responsible for meeting regulations, independent snagging companies like New Home Quality Control argue that inspections are essential. The Home Builders Federation notes that snags are inevitable in bespoke construction but claims quality standards remain high. The UK government has pledged £625m to train 60,000 construction workers to address skills challenges.
items.title: New Home Buyers Face Widespread Defects Despite Inspections

items.summary: EGO Power+ has introduced the LV5005, a battery-powered leaf vacuum, mulcher, and blower designed for fall cleanup. The tool claims 210 mph blowing power and a 16:1 mulching ratio, capable of reducing 16 bags of leaves to one. Arriving for the 2026 season, it features a 6.0 Ah battery offering up to 90 minutes of runtime on low settings.
items.title: EGO Power+ Unveils New Three-in-One Electric Leaf Tool

items.summary: A Mumbai special POCSO court acquitted a 44-year-old Noorbaug teacher accused of sexually assaulting a 16-year-old student in October 2017. The court disbelieved the victim's testimony due to contradictions regarding the timeline and lack of immediate reporting. The defense argued the case was false, stemming from a fee dispute, noting the student continued attending classes and others did too. The court cited major inconsistencies and a two-day delay in filing the FIR as reasons for acquittal.
items.title: Mumbai Court Acquits Teacher in Minor Assault Case

items.summary: The Food Safety Administration in Indore inspected several food establishments near the bus stand area on Saturday. Officials found missing certificates and improper storage at locations like Bharatiya Bhojanalaya and Sai Prasad Dining Hall Restaurant. Teams collected eight food samples, including spices and grains, to be tested at the State Food Testing Laboratory in Bhopal. Improvement notices will be issued based on findings, with further action pending test reports.
items.title: Indore Food Safety Administration Inspects Eateries and Collects Samples

items.summary: Türkiye Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that Ankara championed dialogue and diplomacy over conflict and crisis during the UN General Assembly's high-level week in New York. Fidan, speaking at a news conference, noted that the Turkish delegation raised Israel's policies in Gaza at over 40 bilateral and multilateral engagements. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan also addressed the assembly, focusing on the plight of Palestinians. Fidan highlighted ongoing diplomatic efforts regarding the Strait of Hormuz and regional stability, while reaffirming Türkiye's support for UN reform and its upcoming role as chair of the COP31 climate conference.
items.title: Türkiye Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan Advocates Diplomacy at UN General Assembly

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lourdes to begin the second leg of his four-day France visit, following a historic Mass in Paris that drew roughly 800,000 people. His itinerary includes meetings with French bishops, survivors of sexual abuse, and private audiences. The visit aims to encourage faith in a country where church attendance is declining, despite a recent rise in adult baptisms.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Arrives in Lourdes Following Historic Paris Crowds

items.summary: Wasim El-Haj, a former careers adviser at Sydney Girls High School, has filed a racial discrimination case against the state of New South Wales. He alleges he was directed to stop wearing a keffiyeh, which he views as a symbol of Palestinian struggle. The school principal and department officials cited concerns about causing discord and maintaining political neutrality in schools. El-Haj resigned in March 2025, and the case is scheduled for a hearing on 3 November.
items.title: Palestinian adviser sues NSW over keffiyeh ban

items.summary: The Australian federal government announced the deregistration of the graduate diploma of management (learning) due to concerns it was being misused by non-genuine students to remain in the country. With cancellation set for 5 October, private colleges are offering last-minute discounts to rush students into the course. While current enrolments are permitted to finish, agents are encouraging those with future enrolments to start immediately to maintain visa conditions. Officials warn that suspicious patterns of early commencement will be investigated, noting that the course was part of a wider crackdown on visa-hopping and overstayers.
items.title: Australian Government Cancels Diploma Course Amidst Last-Minute Enrollment Push

items.summary: Goldman Sachs reports that annual technology demand for gold was 323 tonnes in 2025, virtually unchanged from 2024. While AI growth drives chip demand, manufacturers are reducing gold usage through miniaturisation. The electronics sector accounts for around 80% of industrial gold use, with co-packaged optics potentially creating modest future demand.
items.title: Goldman Sachs Analyzes Gold's Role in AI Boom

items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated the plan involved a ceasefire and meeting U.S. demands regarding sanctions and assets. Trump expressed skepticism about Tehran's willingness to comply and indicated potential renewal of bombing campaigns. The strait remains central to the ongoing stalemate between the two nations.
items.title: Trump Rejects Iran's Proposal to Reopen Hormuz Strait

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the United Nations General Assembly, asserting India's right to defend itself against terrorism. He responded to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's criticism of India's Operation Sindoor and accusations regarding human rights. Jaishankar stated that state-sponsored terrorism must be held accountable and that agreements based on friendship cannot coexist with such acts. He also highlighted global conflicts' impact on the Global South and called for a reformed multilateral system.
items.title: India's Jaishankar Condemns Pakistan's Terrorism Claims at UNGA

items.summary: Azerbaijan commemorates Remembrance Day while highlighting six years of peace with Armenia, focusing on post-war recovery and regional integration. Since late 2025, rail freight has resumed, with direct exports reaching over $17 million between January and August 2026. A digital transit agreement now routes Armenian internet traffic through Azerbaijan. High-level diplomacy, including a 2025 Washington summit, formalized the peace framework. Civil society dialogues continue, and Armenia’s Prime Minister received a peace prize in September 2026, acknowledging joint efforts to stabilize the South Caucasus.
items.title: Azerbaijan and Armenia advance peace through trade and digital links

items.summary: A powerful nor'easter has knocked out power to over 100,000 homes and businesses across the US Northeast, grounding hundreds of flights and prompting emergency declarations in New York and New Jersey. High winds and storm surges are expected to worsen conditions, with officials warning of potential flooding and falling trees. The storm has also led to the cancellation of major events and transit suspensions.
items.title: Nor'easter Triggers Emergency Declarations and Widespread Disruptions Across US Northeast

items.summary: The Telangana government ordered the removal of eligible private properties from the Section 22-A prohibited list, benefiting approximately 1.41 lakh homes and plots. Officials stated that over 3.72 lakh acres were inadvertently included during a previous portal update. The move follows political controversy and complaints from owners facing registration blocks. District committees will now scrutinize cases based on valid statutory approvals.
items.title: Telangana Removes Eligible Private Properties from Prohibited 22-A List

items.summary: The Election Commission of India extended deadlines for filing claims and objections under Delhi's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. With 93% of hearings pending and low inclusion applications, the EC directed Booth Level Officers to conduct home verifications. The final roll is scheduled for publication on December 4, 2026.
items.title: Delhi EC extends SIR deadlines amid slow progress

items.summary: The White House barred CNN from traveling with President Donald Trump on Air Force One to a football game in Tennessee. This exclusion followed a note omitting the broadcaster from the schedule, marking a recent escalation in tensions between the administration and media outlets. While a federal judge previously ruled that barring news organizations was likely unconstitutional, the White House continues to restrict access for certain reporters.
items.title: White House Bars CNN From Air Force One Trip

items.summary: Brazil continues expanding renewable energy capacity through favorable policies and foreign investment, achieving a low-carbon mix where renewables account for around 50 per cent of energy. While oil and gas production climbs to strengthen energy security, the nation maintains a strong renewable track record. The World Bank approved a $500 million loan to support clean energy in the Northeast, and Chinese firms are investing in transmission and wind projects. Ahead of October elections, business groups urge candidates to support green growth, though political candidates hold divergent views on fossil fuel expansion. Despite this, Brazil is expected to continue diversifying its energy mix regardless of the election outcome.
items.title: Brazil Expands Green Energy While Oil Production Rises Amid Political Uncertainty

items.summary: According to a report, Boeing informed 737 MAX operators in late August that a software glitch does not pose a safety risk. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The article notes the issue was flagged by Boeing, though the specific details of the glitch and the verification status remain unconfirmed by independent sources at the time of reporting.
items.title: Boeing Reports 737 MAX Software Glitch Without Safety Risk

items.summary: Data cited by The Daily Brief by Zerodha indicates that insurance distribution costs are rising sharply faster than premiums in certain channels. Between FY23 and FY25, remuneration for life corporate agents grew 125% compared to 28% premium growth, while general insurance broker remuneration jumped 173% against 37% premium increases.
items.title: Distributor Payouts Rise Faster Than Premiums in Insurance Channels

items.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots has requested the civil aviation ministry to consider its technical submissions and allow representation in an independent review of the Air India AI 171 crash report before finalisation. The pilots' body, which operates Boeing 787 aircraft, seeks formal inclusion as an independent technical stakeholder in the investigation process.
items.title: Pilots body seeks role in Air India crash probe review

items.summary: Wangchuk issued an unequivocal and unconditional apology for comparing events in Ladakh to those in Tibet. He stated the comparison was inappropriate and aimed at offending Tibetan friends. Wangchuk reiterated his long-standing support for the Tibetan cause, noting his past advocacy for the Dalai Lama and his role in boycotting Chinese products in India. The Central Tibetan Administration responded by labeling the comparison misplaced.
items.title: Wangchuk Apologizes for Inappropriate Tibet Comparison

items.summary: India's Centre ordered over 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at maximum capacity from October 1 through year-end to meet expected rising electricity demand. The directive, issued under emergency provisions of the Electricity Act, applies to plants with at least 50 megawatts installed capacity. Nearly 40% of coal-fired plants currently face critically low fuel stock due to surging demand linked to the El Niño phenomenon. The Ministry of Power also directed generators to sell surplus electricity through power exchanges and extended an earlier order for Tata Power's Mundra plant until December 31.
items.title: Centre Orders Captive Coal Plants to Maximize Output Amid Demand Surge

items.summary: Europe faces growing local opposition to data centers despite their role in digital sovereignty and AI ambitions. Concerns center on high water and electricity consumption, exacerbated by record heat and grid constraints. While operators argue for energy efficiency and waste heat reuse, protests have erupted in locations like Linz and Etrechet. In response, the European Commission announced a transparency scheme for facilities over 500 kW. German officials note that cooling one kilowatt-hour of electricity can use between 0.4 and 4.4 liters of water. Forecasts suggest electricity demand could rise by 40% if current projects proceed.
items.title: Europe faces backlash over data center resource use and local opposition

items.summary: DHL Express announced an 8.9% increase in shipment charges for India effective January 1, 2027. The company attributed the adjustment to inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, and rising operational costs including energy and compliance expenses. RS Subramanian, senior vice president for South Asia, stated the move aims to maintain service levels and strengthen global operational resilience while navigating a complex trade environment.
items.title: DHL Express Announces 8.9% Shipment Charge Hike in India

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar addressed the United Nations General Assembly, invoking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's previous remarks to highlight how countries far from conflicts are being penalised. He urged the assembly to face the true state of affairs, citing ongoing wars in West Asia and Ukraine that impact global energy security and supply chains. Jaishankar called for restraint and a two-state solution for durable peace in the Middle East.
items.title: Jaishankar Invokes Modi's Remarks on Global Conflict Impact at UNGA

items.summary: Dr Lal PathLabs Ltd announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Dr Lal PathLabs FZCO, based in Dubai, has completed the acquisition of an 80 per cent stake in Ghana-based Sunshine Healthcare Ltd. Following the transaction, Sunshine Healthcare Ltd became a step-down subsidiary of Dr Lal PathLabs, according to a regulatory filing. The company stated the deal was finalized in accordance with the agreement and applicable Ghanaian provisions.
items.title: Dr Lal PathLabs Subsidiary Acquires Majority Stake in Ghana Healthcare Firm

items.summary: Ongoing protests in Madrid's Retiro quarter center on the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who lived there since the 1950s. Demonstrators hold signs reading "Maricarmen vs the Vultures" and "Ni una Maricarmen más." The event has sparked broader calls for social protections against a housing deficit. Blame is being shifted between the national government and the Madrid city council regarding the eviction.
items.title: Protests Erupt in Madrid Over Eviction of Elderly Woman

items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has demanded that the Centre confer the Bharat Ratna on former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. Reddy cited Singh's role in forming Telangana and his contribution to India's economic growth. He also urged the government to establish a 'Knowledge Centre' in Delhi to honour Singh's contributions. Reddy made these demands during an event where he unveiled a statue of the former PM in Hyderabad.
items.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Demands Bharat Ratna for Manmohan Singh

items.summary: Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister and Labour leader, pledged to deliver radical change despite severe economic headwinds ahead of the Labour conference in Liverpool. Speaking to the Guardian, he acknowledged challenging public finances and the need for fiscal stability to address larger issues. Burnham addressed global shocks, including the Iran conflict, which have increased inflation and borrowing costs. He ruled out a snap election before 2029 and denied discussions about calling an early one. Burnham also addressed concerns over energy bills, welfare cuts, and political funding, emphasizing honesty and difficult decisions over political spin. He revealed his determination is fueled by his late father's legacy.
items.title: Andy Burnham Pledges Radical Change Amid Economic Challenges

items.summary: Thousands marched in Madrid to protest the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, highlighting rising housing costs and demanding tenant protections. Government authorities estimated 25,000 attendees, while organizers claimed 300,000. Abascal, evicted after rent rose 275%, urges legal changes. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez faces pressure to approve pro-tenant measures, though parliament approval remains uncertain amid a broader housing shortage.
items.title: Thousands March in Madrid to Protest Eviction of Elderly Woman

items.summary: An explosives-laden vehicle rammed a police-customs checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan, killing 13 people and injuring 30. Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the attack. President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the blast, while Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi expressed condolences. Security forces cordoned off the area and launched a search operation as bomb disposal teams investigated the explosives.
items.title: TTP Suicide Attack Kills 13 at Pakistan Checkpost

items.summary: Bihar Police registered a case against a staffer at the Chief Minister's office for posting unblurred photos of a minor girl on the Chief Minister's official account. The Bihar Police stated the post compromised the victim's privacy. Police also filed a case against others for sharing the post and uploading AI-generated videos. Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav accused the Chief Minister of violating the 2012 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.
items.title: Bihar Police Book CM Staffer for Posting Minor's Photo

items.summary: The Election Commission announced on Saturday that the older version of Form 6 will be used for voter registration during periods when the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is not active. Additionally, the commission stated that individuals served notices for being 'unmapped' or having 'logical discrepancies' no longer need to attend mandatory hearings. This decision follows objections by commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi regarding the new form and SIR procedures. The commission clarified that the declaration attached to Form 6 was upheld by the Supreme Court. Meanwhile, the commission also revealed plans to review its IT systems and address concerns over database access.
items.title: Election Commission Reinstates Old Form 6 and Cancels Mandatory Hearings

items.summary: Former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson alleges that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar urged him to contest the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Pathanamthitta as a BJP candidate. Thomson claims Kumar made the offer during a flight while Thomson was still serving as chief secretary, though he declined. Thomson states Kumar insisted several times. The allegation adds to ongoing debates regarding the Election Commission's political neutrality amid criticism over electoral roll revisions. Thomson's account remains unverified by independent evidence.
items.title: Kerala ex-chief secretary alleges CEC urged him to join BJP

items.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray backed a protest call by Abhijeet Dipke against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, stating Mumbai would demonstrate on October 2 if Kumar did not resign. Dipke alleged that over 13 crore votes were deleted and that the SIR process was flawed. The protest follows a report by Indian Express claiming two commissioners objected to decisions made without their knowledge.
items.title: Aaditya Thackeray Supports Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over Vote Chori Allegations

items.summary: Transport experts are questioning whether the Heathrow Express should be discontinued as London prepares for a third runway at Heathrow airport. Under the expansion plan, daily passenger numbers could rise significantly, creating ground congestion and a need for sustainable transport alternatives. Transport for London suggests reviewing the service, noting the Elizabeth line offers a more compelling option for many travelers. While the Heathrow Express remains the fastest connection to central London, it serves a small fraction of total airport passengers. Officials warn that without a clear shift to public transport, the expansion could lead to increased road traffic and taxpayer-funded improvements.
items.title: Experts Question Future of Heathrow Express Amid Airport Expansion

items.summary: A review describes an illustrated book about Abdul Ghaffar Khan, authored by Vazira Zamindar with illustrations by Sarnath Banerjee and design by Veronica Borsani. The text notes the book's scrapbook aesthetic, combining photographs and drawings, which contrasts with its didactic narrative tone. The story follows a Muslim-Hindu couple, Mahmud and Sita, who retrieve a Buddha statue in 1946. The review suggests the book functions as a didactic tale exploring Hindu-Muslim brotherhood and non-violence, though characters remain somewhat distant. It highlights the book's connection to historical events like the 1930 Qissa Khwani Bazaar massacre and links the narrative to broader cultural ties between India and Afghanistan.
items.title: Review of illustrated book on Abdul Ghaffar Khan

items.summary: AFP argues that professional journalism remains essential despite the rise of social media and artificial intelligence. The agency highlights the limitations of citizen journalism and AI-generated content, noting that algorithms often prioritize outrage over truth and can be manipulated by bad actors. AFP points to its rapid response during the Nepal floods, where 11 journalists deployed to document the disaster, contrasting this with the prevalence of deepfake images. The agency emphasizes that gathering facts requires time, expertise, and ethical standards, costs that make professional reporting indispensable for providing reliable information to the world.
items.title: AFP Defends Value of Professional Journalism Against AI and Social Media Challenges

items.summary: A state visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping to the United States drew intense global attention, with every gesture interpreted as a signal of shifting power dynamics. While Trump waited for Xi on a military runway—a rare diplomatic move—analysts noted the lack of substantive dialogue on critical issues like trade and artificial intelligence. The summit appeared more symbolic than substantive, reinforcing perceptions of U.S. dependence on China.
items.title: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump meet in Washington amid global scrutiny

items.summary: Iran proposed a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end regional fighting within seven days, according to a Wall Street Journal report. President Donald Trump rejected the initiative, which Iran presented at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The proposal was transmitted via Qatari mediators and aimed to conclude a conflict that has disrupted global oil flows.
items.title: Trump Rejects Iranian Peace Proposal to End Middle East Fighting

items.summary: Records indicate that in July, cotton shirts from southern Vietnam were unloaded in Los Angeles. These garments originated from a manufacturer closely related to Esquel Group, a Chinese textile giant effectively banned from U.S. sales since November 2024 due to alleged forced labor links in Xinjiang. Despite the ban, three Vietnamese manufacturers with ties to Esquel continued sourcing its cotton and selling products to the U.S. Esquel denies the allegations.
items.title: Firms Linked to Sanctioned Chinese Cotton Giant Sell Clothes to U.S.

items.summary: Secure file-sharing company Kiteworks is urging customers worldwide to temporarily shut down their servers for six hours on Saturday. The precautionary measure follows credible threat intelligence from law enforcement indicating a potential imminent cyberattack. Kiteworks states it is not aware of any confirmed breach but recommends the shutdown to protect against potential zero-day attacks while working with authorities.
items.title: Kiteworks Urges Global Server Shutdown Over Potential Zero-Day Threat

items.summary: GreenYellow commissioned 18 self-consumption photovoltaic plants across Jerónimo Martins sites in Portugal, totaling 8 MWp. The project is expected to generate approximately 11.6 GWh annually and avoid more than 1,230 tonnes of CO₂ emissions. Deployed under a 15-year on-site power purchase agreement, the installations aim to reduce energy cost exposure and support decarbonization objectives for the retail group.
items.title: GreenYellow commissions rooftop solar for Jerónimo Martins sites in Portugal

items.summary: Low Carbon has announced the early-stage development of the West Oxfordshire Energy Park, a proposed 500 MW solar and battery storage project. The developer states the facility could power approximately 145,000 homes and avoid up to 154,000 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. A public consultation is planned for early 2027.
items.title: Low Carbon Announces 500 MW Solar Project in West Oxfordshire

items.summary: An author who previously held skepticism toward OceanX's downwind floating wind design has revised their view following data from Super Typhoon Yagi. Measurements showed the platform maintained stable inclination and tracked simulations closely despite severe wind and wave loading. The author attributes this shift to the engineering of slender, stayed supports and a weather-vaning platform that may mitigate historical downwind fatigue issues. However, the author notes that the twin-rotor configuration remains unconvincing and that economic viability over 25 years remains unproven due to a lack of fatigue and lifecycle data. The analysis suggests the concept deserves fresh consideration, though deeper engineering breakdowns are still required.
items.title: Author Reassesses Downwind Floating Wind After OceanX Typhoon Test

items.summary: The US Department of Energy announced a $99 million funding round on September 21 to support next-generation geothermal energy systems, a move highlighted by President Donald Trump. The initiative targets 21 projects, including 16 for resource exploration and five for technology validation, aiming to reduce technical risks and lower costs. While geothermal currently accounts for about 1% of utility-scale power generation in the US, the funding seeks to expand its role alongside biomass and hydropower under the administration's energy dominance policy. Private sector interest remains high, with companies like Quaise Energy and Sage Geosystems securing additional financing for specific geothermal initiatives.
items.title: US Department of Energy Announces $99 Million Geothermal Funding Boost

items.summary: Justino, an exiled Myanmar journalist and Exile Hub partner, recounts the severe psychological and physical dangers faced since the 2021 coup. He details threats, surveillance, and mental health struggles stemming from investigating human rights violations and armed authorities in regions like Magway and Sagaing. After receiving a death threat in April 2026, he fled to a border area. Despite exhaustion and fear, he remains committed to his work, emphasizing the need for safety measures and the importance of self-care and resilience for journalists.
items.title: Exiled Myanmar Journalist Describes Psychological Toll and Safety Risks
